title: Welcome Screen
summary: Design the first screen of your app: your school’s name, a logo, a welcome message, cards and buttons.

steps.title: Add the school header
steps.objective: Start your welcome screen with a title bar.
steps.concept: The welcome screen is the first thing students see. A header at the top will carry your school’s name.
steps.expected: A title bar appears at the top of the phone.

expect.label: A Header sits in the Header zone of the Welcome screen
expect.fail: Drag the Header tool onto the glowing Header zone.

hints: Find the glowing Header tool in the toolbox on the left.
Drag it onto the dashed strip at the top of the phone.
On a touch screen: tap Header, then tap the glowing Header zone.

steps.title: Type your school’s name
steps.objective: Make the app yours by using your real school name.
steps.concept: The header text becomes the title of your welcome screen. Everyone who opens the app will see it first.
steps.expected: The header shows your school’s name.

expect.label: The header says exactly: Alrowad International Schools
expect.fail: Select the header on the phone, then in Properties → Text content type exactly: Alrowad International Schools

hints: Click the header on the phone to select it.
In the Properties panel, change Text content.
Type your school’s name, then press Check My Work.

steps.title: Add your school logo
steps.objective: Place a logo badge on the screen.
steps.concept: A logo is a round badge that shows your school’s initials. It makes the app feel like it belongs to your school.
steps.expected: A round badge appears in the middle of the phone.

expect.label: A Logo sits in the Body zone
expect.fail: Drag the Logo tool into the Body zone.

hints: The Logo tool is in the toolbox, with a pink badge icon.
Drop it in the large Body zone.
Tap-to-place works too: tap Logo, then tap the Body zone.

steps.title: Put your school name on the logo
steps.objective: Learn that the logo takes its initials from the name you type.
steps.concept: The logo shows the first letters of the words you type. “Al Rowad School” becomes AR.
steps.expected: The logo shows your school’s initials and name.

expect.label: The logo says exactly: Alrowad International Schools
expect.fail: Select the logo on the phone, then in Properties → Text content type exactly: Alrowad International Schools

hints: Click the logo on the phone.
Edit Text content in the Properties panel.
Type your school’s name. The initials update by themselves.

steps.title: Write a welcome message
steps.objective: Add a line of text with a command.
steps.concept: ADD TEXT puts a line of text in the Body zone. Write a friendly message in your own words, inside quotation marks.
steps.expected: Your message appears under the logo.

cmds: ADD TEXT "Welcome to our school app!"

expect.label: The message is exactly: Welcome to our school app!

hints: ADD TEXT adds a line of text.
Put your message inside quotation marks.
For example: ADD TEXT "Welcome to our school app!"

steps.title: Add your first card
steps.objective: Use a card to show one feature of your app.
steps.concept: Cards are blocks that hold one idea each, such as Homework, Timetable or Quiz.
steps.expected: A card appears in the Body zone.

expect.label: A Card sits in the Body zone
expect.fail: Drag the Card tool into the Body zone.

hints: Find the Card tool.
Drop it in the Body zone.
Tap-to-place: tap Card, then tap the Body zone.

steps.title: Name your card
steps.objective: Give the card a name with SET TEXT.
steps.concept: SET TEXT changes the text of the selected component. Choose a feature of your app, such as Homework Helper.
steps.expected: The card shows your own name for it.

expect.label: The card says exactly: Homework Helper

hints: Click the card on the phone first.
Then type SET TEXT and the name in quotation marks.
For example: SET TEXT "Homework Helper"

steps.title: Add two more cards
steps.objective: Show three different features with three different cards.
steps.concept: Each ADD CARD command creates another card. Pick names that tell students what the app can do.
steps.expected: Three cards, each with its own name.

expect.label: There are 3 cards: Homework Helper, My Timetable, Daily Quiz
A card says exactly: Homework Helper
A card says exactly: My Timetable
A card says exactly: Daily Quiz

hints: Type two ADD CARD commands, one per line.
Each name goes in quotation marks.
For example: ADD CARD "My Timetable" and ADD CARD "Daily Quiz"

steps.title: Add the Get Started button
steps.objective: Place a button in the Action bar.
steps.concept: The Get Started button will take students from the welcome screen into the app.
steps.expected: A button appears at the bottom of the phone.

expect.label: A Button sits in the Action bar
expect.fail: Drag the Button tool to the Action bar at the bottom.

hints: Find the Button tool.
Drop it on the Action bar strip at the bottom.
Tap-to-place: tap Button, then tap the Action bar.

steps.title: Label the button
steps.objective: Give the button a clear label.
steps.concept: We will use the exact label Get Started, because the next steps find the button by its label.

expect.label: The button says Get Started
expect.fail: Select the button and set Text content to exactly: Get Started

hints: Click the button on the phone.
Change Text content in the Properties panel.
Type exactly: Get Started

steps.title: Add a second button
steps.objective: Use another button for a different job.
steps.concept: A welcome screen can offer more than one choice, such as About Us or Contact. Choose a label that fits your school.
steps.expected: A second button appears in the Action bar.

expect.label: The second button says exactly: About Us

hints: ADD BUTTON adds a button to the Action bar.
The label goes in quotation marks.
For example: ADD BUTTON "About Us"

steps.title: Link Get Started to Home
steps.objective: Make the button open another screen.
steps.concept: LINK BUTTON sends the user to a screen when they tap. The Home screen is the dashboard of your finished app, which the studio builds for you.

expect.label: Get Started is linked to Home

hints: LINK BUTTON needs the button label and the screen name.
Both go in quotation marks, with the word TO between.
Exactly: LINK BUTTON "Get Started" TO "Home"

steps.title: Final style check: every colour, border, shadow and style
steps.objective: Give your screens the same colours, shapes and shadows as the model app.
steps.concept: Colours were chosen while you built each element. Now finish the whole look: every colour, background, border, corner, shadow and text style below must match the model app you tried at the start. Items you already set show a tick.
steps.expected: Your screens look exactly like the model app.
hints: Click the element on the phone first. The style box (Choose colours, borders and corners) opens by itself.
Follow the sub-steps one by one: each says which row to use and which option to click. The red dot shows where.
Text alignment and weight are in the Properties panel (right) under “Text and layout”.

steps.title: Run and test your welcome screen
steps.objective: Use your screen like a student would.
steps.concept: Run Project turns the phone into a working app. The studio first shows a short demo of your buttons, then you can tap them yourself.
steps.expected: Tapping Get Started opens the Home dashboard.

expect.name: ran
expect.fail: Press Run Project in the top bar.
expect.label: You pressed Run Project

expect.name: nav:home
expect.label: You tapped Get Started and saw the Home screen
expect.fail: In the running app, tap Get Started yourself. If nothing happens, check the link you made in step 12.

subs.t: Press Run Project in the top bar
Watch the demo, then tap Get Started yourself

hints: Press Run Project and watch the demo.
Tap the Get Started button on the phone.
The Home dashboard should appear.

objectives: Design the first screen students see: your school’s name, a logo and a welcome message.
Use cards and buttons, and link a button to the Home screen.
Choose your own colours, then run the screen like a real student.

mcqs.q: What is the main job of the first screen of an app?
a: Welcome the user and show where to go next
mcqs.why: The first screen gives a friendly start and a clear next action.

mcqs.q: Which tool puts a round badge with the school's initials on a screen?
mcqs.why: A logo helps users recognise the school or app at a glance.

mcqs.q: Why are cards used for the main sections on a welcome screen?
a: Each card holds one item and is easy to see and tap
Cards make the app load faster
Cards are the only way to add text
mcqs.why: Cards group one idea each, so the screen stays tidy.

mcqs.q: What does a command like LINK BUTTON do?
a: Connects a button to the screen it should open
mcqs.why: Commands are typed instructions that tell the app what to do.

mcqs.q: What is the best way to check that a button works?
a: Run the project and tap it like a real user
mcqs.why: Only running the app shows what a user will really experience.
